profile.name: Cantarella
profile.introduction: The current head of Fisalia, Cantarella, the Bane. A mysterious noblewoman, her beauty as captivating as it is perilous. She resides in a crown-like castle perched atop the mountain, where illusory dreams flow like streams, meticulously spun by her own hands.
profile.review:
Cantarella is a 5-star Havoc Rectifier Hybrid and Sustain character who first introduced the Echo Skill Cast mechanic. Indeed, Cantarella is able to cast 3 more Echo Skills than normal through some attacks that are counted as such. On top of this, she has some Outro buffs tailored towards her best DPS to pair with, being Phrolova, and features some Sustain capabilities to boot.

Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts

Cantarella’s main gimmick is her ability to cast 4 total Echo Skills throughout her rotation. The skills that do so are as follows (1 cast each):

  • Her Ultimate;

  • Her regular Skill in Mirage form (we explain this afterwards);

  • Her Forte Skill in Mirage form;

  • Her regular active Echo Skill (the same way anyone else could).

To explain what the Mirage state is, Cantarella enters it through casting a special Heavy Attack called Delusive Dive. She gains access to it when she has at least 1 Forte point, called Trance. She gains it through the following abilities:

  • Her Intro (1 point);

  • Her Skill (1 point);

  • Her Basic 3 (1 point);

  • Her Ultimate (3 points).

She then consumes these stacks in Mirage state through the new Basic Attacks that she unlocks. She also gains access to a new Skill (that counts as an extra Echo Skill cast). That Skill has the special property of sending all enemies hit by it into a slow-down state for 6.5s, interrupted if any character hits them. If Cantarella does so, an extra damage multiplier is triggered.

Once 3 Trance stacks have been consumed in Mirage state, Cantarella gains access to a Forte Skill called Perception Drain. It deals a lot of damage, heals the party a significant amount, and generates a lot of Concerto on top of counting as an extra Echo Skill cast.

Cantarella also has a passive that’s necessary to her Concerto generation that operates on a 25s basis, called “Abyssal Rebirth”. When Cantarella casts an Intro, she enters this state and restores 6 Concerto per Echo Skill cast of herself and her teammates, up to 6 times. This is necessary in order for her to complete her rotations.

Lastly, Cantarella’s Ultimate also generates up to 21 Coordinated Attacks, triggered once every second at maximum, though they deal close to no damage. Her Outro Skill is the only source of buffing in her kit, granting the next character that Cantarella switches into 20% Havoc and 25% Skill DMG Amplification for 14s, expiring on swap.

In short, Cantarella’s rotation has her quickly generating Concerto and Trance through her base Skill and Ultimate, then entering Mirage state to cast her Skill and 3 Basic Attacks into Perception drain before switching out. She is simplistic gameplay-wise and easy to pick up.

Meta Position & Conclusion

Cantarella’s position in the meta is one of the most unfortunate in Wuthering Waves. Phrolova has been one of the most meta-relevant characters since her release, and Cantarella has always been one of her best teammates. However, the Echo Skill engine got expanded upon significantly not long after Phrolova’s release. While this has resulted in significant teammate upgrades for Phrolova in the form of Lucilla and Qiuyuan, that also means Cantarella fell out of fashion in the only team where she was best. While Cantarella’s own best team remains the one with Phrolova, Phrolova’s own best team doesn’t even include Cantarella in it anymore.

In other words, Cantarella’s currently in a position where if you have Phrolova, you’re forced to use them together simply because Cantarella has no other meta use cases, even if she isn’t ideal for Phrolova’s own team anymore. That said, Lucilla and Qiuyuan are very high-value teammates that can be used with Sigrika or Hiyuki instead, for example. And that’s where Cantarella comes in. 

Nonetheless, calling Cantarella powercrept is an accurate statement. Due to a lack of buffs outside her Outro, she’s useless for Echo Skill characters that don’t make use of it. Due to replaceability by Lucilla and Qiuyuan that exceed her, but also Lynae, Roccia and even Danjin that get very close to her level of performance, Cantarella isn’t part of Phrolova’s best in slot and has stayed replaceable since her release. Due to her rotation operating on a 25-second cooldown, her Coordinated Attacks that should make her synergistic with Jinhsi don’t actually extend her team flexibility in practice (as Jinhsi can’t rotate normally by making use of Unison like she could with Zhezhi or Yinlin).

In conclusion, Cantarella is still good for Phrolova teams, but she definitely pays the price in terms of team flexibility. Cantarella only exists in the Phrolova team at this point, for whom she is not even best in slot anymore, provided you have Lucilla and Qiuyuan both available. If you don’t, Cantarella is still your best bet for your Phrolova teams. However, existing in a powercrept state, with a lack of team flexibility and staying power, whilst being replaceable by accessible options, definitely calls her current pull value into question. If you own her and have Phrolova, great news as she’ll be very serviceable, but for beginners and players who skipped her, we do not recommend Cantarella currently.
profile.pros:
• Extra Echo Skill casts and an ideal Outro to buff Phrolova, a very meta-relevant DPS to date;

  • Has Sustain capabilities, which none of Phrolova’s other ideal teammates have.
profile.cons:
• Literally only a good choice for Phrolova teams, significantly outclassed by Qiuyuan and Lucilla in the Echo Skill buffing department - even for Phrolova teams if you don’t care about the healing. Also outclassed by many other buffers for Havoc/Skill teams in general, so her team flexibility is nonexistent;

  • Big Energy Regen problems - Cantarella generates very little Resonance Energy for the team and herself. Her and her team’s Energy Regen requirements can spike (not Phrolova/Lucilla since they don’t require any Energy though);

  • Could be distracting to play for many (not our case, but no judging if you recognized yourself).

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Cantarella’s rotation goal is to build up to her Outro as quickly as possible while ensuring she has cast all of her Echo Skills. Below are all the different ways you can do so based on your use case.

Echo Timing

Considering Cantarella only ever uses Transform Echoes, and she needs to cast them after her Intro due to Abyssal Rebirth mechanics, her Echo timings have been written directly into her rotations.

Important: The rotations below are written for general use. In Phrolova teams, to take maximum advantage of Hecate’s Enhanced Attacks cast by Cantarella, her active Echo cast should be interrupted via Dash & Ultimate, but Cantarella should still remain on-field while casting Perception Drain. Only switch out once the attack landed.

Fastest Rotation

This is the fastest possible rotation that preserves the majority of Cantarella's quickly dealt damage, maximizing DPS at the cost of very low Energy generation.

  • Intro: Ripple

  • Skill: Graceful Step (Instantly interrupt via Echo)

  • Echo (Instantly interrupt via Dash)

  • Dash (Instantly interrupt via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Heavy: Delusive Dive

  • Skill: Flickering Reverie

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 1

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 2

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 3 (Instantly interrupt via Skill)

  • Skill: Perception Drain (Swap)

  • Outro

Standard Rotation

This rotation serves as a middle-ground between a fully extended and the fastest possible Cantarella rotation, retaining Perception Drain on-field for Outro buffs like Roccia's while preserving the decent Energy generation and damage of the Echo cast.

  • Intro: Ripple

  • Skill: Graceful Step (Instantly interrupt via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Heavy: Delusive Dive

  • Skill: Flickering Reverie

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 1

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 2

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 3 (Instantly interrupt via Skill)

  • Skill: Perception Drain

  • Echo (Swap)

  • Outro

Extended Rotation

Fully extended Cantarella rotation that makes the most of her Damage Per Rotation. Takes significantly longer, can prove situationally useful with Sequences/specific teams.

  • Intro: Ripple

  • Basic 3 (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill: Graceful Step (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Heavy: Delusive Dive

  • Skill: Flickering Reverie

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 1

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 2

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 3 (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill: Perception Drain

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 1

  • Basic: Phantom Sting 2 (Cancel animation endlag via Echo)

  • Echo (Swap)

  • Outro

skills.name: Illusion Collapse
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Havoc DMG.

Heavy Attack

Consume STA to attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG.

Heavy Attack - Delusive Dive

When Cantarella has Trance, Heavy Attack becomes Delusive Dive, dealing Havoc DMG to the target, and then Cantarella enters Mirage. While in Mirage, casting Delusive Dive does not activate Mirage again. Can be cast in water.

Mid-air Attack

Consume STA to perform Plunging Attack, dealing Havoc DMG.

Dodge Counter

Press Normal Attack right after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG.

skills.name: Dance with Shadows
skills.description:
Graceful Step

Attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG.

Flickering Reverie

When in Mirage, Resonance Skill becomes Flickering Reverie, which is considered an Echo Skill when being cast. Attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG, and send them into Hazy Dream.

Can be cast in mid-air.

Hazy Dream

Reduce the target's movement speed for 6.5s. When the target takes damage, Jolt is triggered once, removing Hazy Dream to deal Havoc DMG, considered Basic Attack DMG. Attacks by other Resonators in the team will not Jolt a target influenced by Hazy Dream and will remove the Hazy Dream.

Coordinated Attacks and damage from Utilities will not Jolt a target.

skills.name: Beneath the Sea
skills.description:
Flowing Suffocation

Attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG (considered Basic Attack DMG). Grant Diffusion to all Resonators in the team. Casting this skill is also considered as casting Echo Skill.

Can be cast in mid-air close to the ground.

Diffusion

When the Resonator on the field deals damage to a target, summon Dreamweavers to perform Coordinated Attack, dealing Havoc DMG (considered as Basic Attack DMG).

  • Within 3s after the Resonator deals damage, summon 1 Dreamweaver per second. This effect can be triggered once per second. Damage dealt by Dreamweavers cannot trigger this effect.

  • Up to 1 Dreamweaver can be summoned each second, max 21 Dreamweavers in total.

  • This effect lasts for 30s or until reaching the maximum number of Dreamweavers.

skills.name: Between Illusion and Reality
skills.description:
Mirage

  • Basic Attack becomes Basic Attack Phantom Sting. Perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Havoc DMG. Can be cast in mid-air. When cast mid-air, Basic Attack Phantom Sting consumes STA, and the combo does not reset when Cantarella is airborne.

  • Hitting the target with Basic Attack Phantom Sting consumes 1 point of Trance to obtain 1 point of Shiver and heal all nearby Resonators in the team.

  • The third stage of Basic Attack Phantom Sting triggers 3 Coordinated Attacks, dealing Havoc DMG.

  • Mid-air Attack becomes Abysmal Vortex. Press Jump to perform a Plunging Attack at the cost of STA, dealing Havoc DMG.

  • Dodge Counter becomes Dodge Counter Shadowy Sweep. Attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG. Press Normal Attack right after casting the skill to cast Basic Attack Phantom Sting Stage 2.

  • When Mid-air Attack Abysmal Vortex or Dodge Counter Shadowy Sweep hits a target, consume 1 point of Trance to obtain 1 point of Shiver and heal all nearby Resonators in the team.

  • Mirage lasts for 8s.

  • Mirage ends when Trance is depleted.

Forte Circuit - Perception Drain

  • If Cantarella has 3 points of Shiver when in Mirage, Resonance Skill becomes Perception Drain.

  • Consume all Shiver to attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG, considered Basic Attack DMG. Send the target into Hazy Dream and heal all Resonators in the team.

  • Casting this skill is also considered as casting Echo Skill.

  • Can be cast in mid-air.

Abyssal Rebirth

  • After casting Intro Skill, Cantarella enters Abyssal Rebirth, which lasts for 25s and can be activated once every 25s. In the duration, for up to 6 times, when Resonators in the team cast Echo Skill, Cantarella recovers 6 points of Concerto Energy. Echoes with the same name can only trigger this effect once.

  • When in water, Cantarella's swimming speed increases and STA cost decreases.

Trance

  • Cantarella can hold up to 5 points of Trance.

  • Casting Intro Skill recovers 1 point of Trance.

  • Hitting a target with Basic Attack Stage 3 recovers 1 point of Trance.

  • Casting Resonance Skill Graceful Step recovers 1 point of Trance.

  • Casting Resonance Liberation Flowing Suffocation recovers 3 point of Trance.

  • When in the water, recover 1 point of Trance every 5s.

Shiver

  • Cantarella can hold up to 3 points of Shiver.

  • Hitting the target with Basic Attack Phantom Sting recovers 1 point of Shiver.

  • When Mid-air Attack Abysmal Vortex or Dodge Counter Shadowy Sweep hits a target, restore 1 point of Shiver.

Important!

  • Sequence 3: Cantarella's Sequence 3 allows her Ultimate to initiate Mirage, allowing you to skip using Delusive Dive if you so desire. Trimming Delusive Dive from the rotation can result in an increase in DPS beyond what is displayed below.

weapons.Comment: Cantarella's signature weapon is expectedly perfect for her, as it gives her a huge boost to many stats including CRIT DMG, ATK, Basic ATK DMG Bonus and can even ignore Havoc RES. These buffs activate naturally quickly in her rotation, making the weapon especially powerful.

Cantarella can make great use of the passive effects of Zhezhi's signature weapon since she heavily benefits from Basic Attack DMG Bonus. It also has CRIT DMG and ATK% - 2 stats Cantarella enjoys as a damage dealer. Having 3 uses of her Resonance Skill, Cantarella is able to exploit this weapon's passive effects well too. This makes this option an outstanding choice for her if you own it.

Yinlin's signature weapon is a versatile option that gives a lot great stats such as CRIT Rate, All-Type DMG Bonus and ATK, especially if the character deals off-field damage or uses Swap Cancels. Because of this, it almost always lands as the #1 or #2 weapon of choice for rectifier damage dealers. On Cantarella specifically, it's about equal to Zhezhi's Signature since she uses its passive well.

While this weapon theoretically could provide 8% DEF Ignore to Cantarella in teams where she can Swap Cancel it before casting her Intro, in practice in her best teams since Outro buffs will be active on all 3 team members at once this passive rarely sees any use since interrupting an Echo cast's damage for it is not worth it. Hence, it mostly acts as a CRIT Rate and ATK stat-stick for Cantarella.
Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Cantarella, who doesn't benefit from this weapon's Spectro Frazzle-related effects.

Best permanently available option for most Rectifier damage dealers, particularly useful on Cantarella since it provides Basic Attack DMG and Energy Regen via its passive, which are stats that Cantarella particularly benefits from.

This Battle Pass exclusive sports a very useful CRIT DMG stat as well as an ATK and Basic ATK DMG Bonus boost when casting any Skill via its passive, which Cantarella can greatly benefit from, making this the best 4-star choice. Still outclassed by any 5-stars due to a lower Base ATK.

This Battle Pass exclusive sports a very useful CRIT Rate stat as well as an ATK boost when casting Ultimate, which makes it very generally usable and a great 4-star choice for Rectifier damage dealers.

The best non-Battle Pass 4-star for Cantarella as it gives her some flat Resonance Energy which means she needs much less Energy Regen on her build to work, however only increasing ATK isn't enough to make it stand out above other options.

Best fully F2P-accessible option, selectable for free at the start of the game or obtained through gacha. Gives a lot of ATK% via its stats and its passive activated upon Intro, but doesn't provide anything else, not making it stand out over the above options.

echoes.Comment: Best set for Cantarella in all Havoc teams. Offers a 10% unconditional Havoc DMG% boost alongside adding a large Havoc Damage hit to the Outro of the wearer. Also grants the incoming resonator a Havoc DMG% boost when the wearer uses their Outro.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Cantarella's best Echo that gives her 12% Havoc and 12% Basic Attack DMG in the main slot. Considering this is a Transform Echo, it has to be used before her rotation ends and must be Swap Cancelled to minimize her rotation time.

echoes.Comment: Best set for Cantarella in all non-Havoc teams. This set sacrifices Cantarella's personal damage in order to provide higher buffing to a single character. It provides an extra 10% Energy Regen to the wielder unconditionally and gives 22.5% ATK to the incoming character for 15s after casting Outro skill, making it one of the strongest sets to buff any ATK-scaling DPS.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: The best and only real option 5P Moonlit Clouds has, as it grants an extra 12% DMG Bonus on top of the ATK boost to the next character that Moonlit Clouds would usually give. Additionally restores a lot of Energy to the caster when it deals damage. On Cantarella, this Echo should either be used before her rotation starts or it can be instantly interrupted via her Ultimate - this way, no Energy or damage is generated but the buff will still apply to the incoming ally.

echoStats.Name: cantarella
echoStats.Substats: Energy Regen (Until Satisfied) > CRIT RATE = CRIT DMG > ATK% > ATK = Basic ATK DMG%

skillPriority.Order: Forte Circuit, Res. Skill, Res. Liberation, Basic Attack, Intro Skill
skillPriority.Comments: Basic and Intro can be skipped when levelling to save on resources at a minimal damage loss.

teams.Name: Team #3: Skill Damage Teams
teams.Comments: Cantarella wielding Moonlit Clouds is significantly stronger than other options to alleviate Energy requirements. Expect the paired DPS character to need higher Energy Regen than usual to function.

synergies.Comment: Cantarella is easily Phrolova's best teammate as she amplifies her Havoc and Skill DMG via her Outro, takes a good amount of field time while doing good damage, and a lot of her actions are counted as Echo skills, providing 3 extra Echo skill attacks per rotation. This allows Phrolova to cast more Enhanced attacks and buff herself further. Not only that, but Cantarella's flaw being Energy generation doesn't matter to Phrolova as she doesn't have any Resonance Energy to begin with. A perfect pair.

Cantarella can also be used as a subtitute for the dedicated Supports of Skill damage dealers, in this niche Carlotta and Jinhsi are the stand-out options. Jinhsi can also make use of Cantarella's Coordinated Attacks, however Cantarella's really low Energy generation makes Energy requirements on her teams really high so in both cases she's outclassed by Zhezhi (or even Yinlin in Jinhsi's case).

As the two best generalist Supports by heaps and bounds, it's no surprise Shorekeeper and Verina can slot in almost any team in the game as they provide high team-wide ATK% and 15% DMG Amplify. Shorekeeper additionally provides CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG, always making a great generalist third slot teammate choice for Cantarella teams, but Verina is a close, more accessible second provided Shorekeeper isn't available.
